(p-195)Surah At-Takathur (The Rivalry in World Increase)

Meccan, though its status is disputed, and its verses number eight.

﴿Rivalry in worldly increase diverts you﴾ — that is, the competition for abundance and boasting about it has occupied you. It is narrated that the clans of Banu 'Abd Manaf and Banu Sahm boasted against each other, counted their numbers, and vied with one another in multiplying their noble leaders and dignitaries in Islam. Each of the two groups said: "We are greater than you in leaders, mightier in our mighty ones, and more numerous in our men." Banu 'Abd Manaf outnumbered them, so Banu Sahm said: "Indeed, rebellion (al-baghy) has consumed us in the Jahiliyyah," and so they counted against them with the living and the dead, and Banu Sahm outnumbered them. The meaning is: you have competed in multiplying through the living.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 102, verse 2:

﴿Until you visited the graves﴾ That is: until, when you have exhausted counting them, you proceed to boasting and vying with one another in the dead. He expressed their reaching (the graves) by mentioning the dead through visiting the graves, as mockery of them. It was also said: they used to visit the graves and say, "This is the grave of so-and-so, and this is the grave of so-and-so," taking pride in that. It was also said that the meaning is: "The competition for more (wealth) in possessions and children has distracted you until you died and were buried, having wasted your lives in the pursuit of this world, turning away from what should concern you of striving for your Hereafter." In this case, visiting the graves is an expression for death. It was also read as "Aalhākum" (أألهاكم) in the interrogative form of affirmation (al-istifham al-taqriri).

"Kallā" (indeed not; a rebuke and a warning) indicates that the sensible person should not have the greater part of his concern confined to this world, for the outcome of that is grim. ﴿Soon you will know﴾ the evil consequence of what you are upon when you witness its end.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 102, verse 4:

﴿Then no! Soon you will know﴾ is a repetition for emphasis. The "then" (thumma) indicates that the second is more emphatic than the first. Or, the first is at death or in the grave, and the second is at the resurrection (nushur).

ۚ﴿Kalla, law ta'lamuna 'ilm al-yaqin﴾ (No! If only you knew with the certainty of knowledge)

That is: if you knew what lies before you with the knowledge of certainty, i.e., like your knowledge of what you are certain of, you would do what cannot be described or fully comprehended. The answer (jawab) to the conditional has been omitted for the sake of awe-inspiring magnification (al-tahwil).

The Almighty's saying: ﴿You will surely see the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim)﴾ is the answer to an implied oath (qasam mudmar), by which the threat was emphasized for them, the warning was intensified, and what they had been warned of, after its vagueness, was made clear, as a matter of magnification.

Then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty.

﴿Then you will surely see it﴾: witnessing and direct observation. ﴿with the eye of certainty﴾: that is, the sight which is the very essence of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn), for knowledge gained by direct witnessing is the highest degree of certainty.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 102, verse 8:

﴿Then you will surely be asked on that Day about the pleasure (al-na'im).﴾ That is: about the pleasure that the enjoyment of worldly delights diverted you from religion and its obligations. The address is specific to those who devote their resolve to pursuing pleasures, who live only to eat good food and wear soft clothing, and who spend their time in amusement and merriment, paying no heed to knowledge and action and not burdening themselves with their hardships. As for one who enjoys the blessing of Allah the Exalted and is strengthened by it to obey Him, and who rises up in gratitude, he is far removed from this. It has also been said: the verse is specific to the disbelievers.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat al-Takathur, Allah will not hold him to account for the blessings He bestowed upon him in the world, and he will be given a reward as if he had recited a thousand verses."
